answer: Private canary tokens expose identities that share one memory. Each seat's tasks carry secret strings unique to it, such as a fictional onyx quarry code or a nectar yield figure, logged by the network under that seat's key. A shared model session acts as a prism, refracting one context into many personas, so a canary planted in seat A eventually surfaces in seat B's output; both are flagged and lose their 500 POA bonds. To run 200 fakes safely, an operator needs 200 fully isolated contexts plus 200 bonds, and one leak burns every linked seat.
